case_name: Upendra Pratapsingh Rajput @ Golu v. Smt. Sanju Rajput Wife Of Upendra

parties.respondent_defendant: Smt. Sanju Rajput Wife Of Upendra, wife

facts_of_case: Petitioner/husband challenging the order dated 13.10.2022 passed by Principal Judge, Family Court, District Raisen in HMA No.54/2018.

legal_principles.principle: In a petition seeking judicial separation, an allegation of adultery by the spouse with a third party is required to be adjudicated.
legal_principles.held: The High Court in exercise of power under sections 14 and 21 of the Hindu Marriage Act , 1955 has framed Rules. Under Rule 2(7)(e)(2) of the Rules, in a petition seeking dissolution of marriage on the ground of adultery, the date and place of the adultery and the name and address of the person with whom the adultery was committed by the respondent is required to be stated.
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — for establishing the importance of adjudicating allegations in judicial separation petitions

legal_principles.principle: A person whose reputation is likely to be affected by a finding recorded in a suit should have an opportunity to defend their reputation before such a finding is recorded.
legal_principles.held: The aforesaid Rule [Rule 5] enjoins a duty on the Court to issue notice to the respondent and co-respondent, if any. The principle is that such a person should have an opportunity to defend his reputation before such a finding is recorded.
applicable_acts_sections: Rules of the M.P. High Court
legal_principles.significance: MEDIUM — for highlighting the importance of natural justice in family law cases

outcome.final_order: The court set aside the order of the trial court directing the petitioner to implead Suryapratap Singh Rajput @ Sonu Rajput as party to the petition filed under Section 10 of The Hindu Marriage Act for judicial separation.
